transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-09
Start: 14:00 EST
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Mark Evans (CTO - Brookline), Lisa Chen (Head of ML), Daniel Park (Infra Lead)

Summary: initial discovery focused on Dedicated/reserved capacity for Brookline's inference workload, isolation and compliance needs (VPC, KMS), burst strategy for peak trading hours, scaling expectations, and next steps to run a benchmark pilot.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Alex Morgan from Redwood, and with me is Priya our solutions engineer. Quick round robin?
[00:08] Mark: Hi, Mark Evans from Brookline, CTO. We, uh, Lisa and Daniel are here too.
[00:13] Lisa: Lisa Chen, head of ML.
[00:15] Daniel: Daniel Park, infra.
[00:18] Alex: Great. High level - we heard you're evaluating dedicated capacity, isolation, burst, that sort of thing. Priya will do a bit on capacity and autoscaling after we cover requirements.
[00:26] Mark: Yeah, we've been running batch and a few online ops on cloud VMs, but latency at peak is rough and costs are spiking. We're interested in reserved GPUs, predictable throughput and keeping sensitive data inside our VPC.
[00:38] Priya: Sounds good. Can you share current QPS and p95/p99 targets? Also models - are these LLM chat-style, embeddings, or encoders?
[00:47] Lisa: Mostly a customer-support assistant and some document ingestion flows. Main model is an Llama variant - 13B - being used for both chat generation and reranking. We target p95 under 350 ms for shorter prompts, but we can tolerate up to 1s for longer context. Peak QPS around 60 requests/sec during morning window.
[01:08] Alex: Okay that's useful. Dedicated can give you reserved GPU pools; you can pin model versions and get data isolation. We offer VPC peering, customer KMS integration, and audit logs.
[01:18] Daniel: About that KMS - do you support customer-managed keys? And we need logs retained for 7 years for audits.
[01:25] Alex: Yes, we support customer KMS/HSM integrations. Audit logs - retention is an add-on, but we can configure longer retention for enterprise accounts. We'll share the SOC 2/ISO docs.
[01:34] Lisa: Cost is a big question. How do you handle burst to meet peaks without paying for reserved capacity 24/7?
[01:41] Priya: Great question. We offer a reserved pool for baseline capacity and a burst tier for handling spikes. Burst can be from the same pool with autoscaling rules or via transient cloud instances depending on deployment mode. For Dedicated we can provision burst capacity in the same datacenter/region - latency impact is minimal if configured correctly.
[02:00] Mark: When you say autoscaling, is it vertical or horizontal? How fast can you scale to 8 GPUs if baseline is 4?
[02:07] Priya: It's horizontal within the GPU fleet. Scaling time depends on cold-start image time, loading model weights, and KV cache warmup. Typical warm-up for a 13B quantized model is around 60-180 seconds to be ready, but we use KV cache preloading to reduce tail latency. We can also keep standby instances if you want faster bursts at cost.
[02:28] Daniel: Is the KV cache shared across requests or per-request? We want to avoid cache leakage between tenants.
[02:34] Priya: KV cache is per-instance and isolated per-tenant when in Dedicated; we also support explicit cache partitioning. There might be some notes in the docs where the transcription sometimes shows K V cache spelled out by auto-transcription.
[02:45] Mark: Right. Another red flag is failover - what's the model variant fallback if a node fails? We need graceful degradation.
[02:52] Alex: Default is automatic fallback to a compatible model variant in the same pool or to hosted variants in a different tier if requested. You can set policies: strict (no fallback), degrade-latency (fallback to smaller model), or replicate (keep warm standby).
[03:07] Lisa: For our use case, quality is important; we can't drop to a tiny 1.3B unless it's only for short, non-critical flows. We need to be able to A/B and canary rollouts.
[03:18] Priya: We support canary and rollout policies through the console, with traffic split and automatic rollback on regressions. We also integrate eval hooks to monitor output quality.
[03:27] Mark: Security questions - SSO/SAML integration, RBAC, and network egress must be controlled. Do you support private deployments or VPC-only control plane?
[03:36] Alex: For Dedicated we offer a private control plane with VPC peering; for full isolation, Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) gives you a customer-managed control plane. SSO/SAML and SSO group sync are supported, plus fine-grained RBAC.
[03:49] Daniel: What about compliance for financial services - will your SOC 2 report and encryption at rest be enough?
[03:55] Alex: SOC 2 + customer-managed KMS typically satisfies most audits; we'll send the SOC 2 report and a security pack. For stricter needs, Private deployment or on-prem with HSM options is available.
[04:07] Lisa: On inference performance: do you support quantized models? We already quantize 4-bit for cost.
[04:13] Priya: Yes, runtime is optimized for quantization-friendly execution paths. We recommend profiles based on model and workload - quantization plus batching yields big costs savings. We'll recommend kernel/config choices after seeing your trace.
[04:26] Mark: About batching - we need low latency. How do you balance batching and p95 targets?
[04:31] Priya: We do continuous batching with latency-aware batching thresholds; you can configure maximum batch size and latency SLOs. For sub-350ms p95, we typically keep small batch windows and use prefix caching to cut effective compute.
[04:42] Daniel: Can we route requests so that high-priority traffic always lands on reserved GPUs and lower-priority on hosted?
[04:48] Alex: Yes - smart routing policies let you prioritize by route, model, or token budget. We can route by customer tier so mission-critical routes use Dedicated reserved capacity and fall back to hosted only if allowed.
[05:00] Lisa: We want to run a pilot with 4 GPUs baseline and ability to burst to 8, and run real traffic for two weeks. What's the typical timeline?
[05:07] Alex: Pilot can start in ~2 weeks once we sign an MSA and set up VPC peering and keys. Priya will run a benchmark with your model.
[05:14] Priya: For the benchmark we'll need a sample inference set, expected QPS peaks, and network config. We'll do latency and cost per-token breakdown and a KV cache warmup plan.
[05:25] Mark: That sounds good. A few more technical clarifications: are there GPU affinity constraints? We run mixed workloads in our infra and want to avoid noisy neighbors.
[05:33] Priya: Dedicated pools are isolated at the tenant level. If you require single-tenant machines (no co-tenancy), we can provision dedicated hosts - it's typically part of the Private or an enterprise Dedicated add-on.
[05:43] Daniel: For autoscaling policies, can we set scheduled scaling for market open times?
[05:47] Priya: Yep, scheduled scaling is supported - you can have baseline reserved plus scheduled increases and dynamic autoscale on top.
[05:55] Mark: How do you measure and bill cache hits vs compute? There was a place in pricing that mentioned token billing and separate charges for persistent KV storage?
[06:02] Alex: Billing is per-token for generation + per-embedding units where applicable; Dedicated has a monthly capacity charge for reserved GPUs plus usage for burst and optional storage/observability add-ons. We'll send a pricing breakdown showing examples for your workload.
[06:12] Lisa: Can we get per-request traces to tie errors to prompts?
[06:16] Priya: Yes, Redwood Console provides per-request tracing, token-level cost breakdowns, and error logs; you can forward traces to your observability stack.
[06:23] Mark: Let's talk about SLAs - what's the uptime and latency SLAs for Dedicated?
[06:28] Alex: We offer SLA-backed uptime targets for Dedicated; latency SLOs are contractable. We'll include SLA language in the enterprise docs.
[06:35] Lisa: Any limitations on model size? We plan to try a 70B down the road.
[06:39] Priya: We support up to large-parameter models; for 70B you'll likely want model sharding/multi-GPU serving and we can advise on cluster configs and quantization strategy.
[06:48] Mark: On the networking side - do you support private egress or forced egress through our gateways?
[06:53] Alex: You can control egress via VPC peering and NAT setups; Private deployments can be air-gapped if needed.
[07:00] Daniel: For the pilot, we'll need an NDA and outline of data handling.
[07:03] Alex: We'll circulate NDA and an MSA template.
[07:06] Lisa: About monitoring - can we get quality-regression alerts tied to prompt evals?
[07:11] Priya: Yes, Redwood Optimize ties eval sets to production outputs and triggers alerts on regressions; we can hook that into your slack or pager.
[07:18] Mark: Any notable limitations or gotchas you recommend we watch for?
[07:21] Priya: Main ones are warm-up times for large models if you don't keep warm standbys, and the tradeoff between burst readiness and cost. Also network egress setup can take some coordination.
[07:33] Mark: Good. Competitors - we've looked at SageMaker and Vertex. Why Redwood vs those?
[07:39] Alex: Customers choose Redwood for production-first inference controls - latency/cost levers, unified interface across hosted/dedicated/private, and transparent perf profiles. We'll share benchmarks that show throughput/latency tradeoffs.
[07:50] Lisa: If we do a pilot, can we try both quantized and non-quantized variants to compare quality?
[07:55] Priya: Absolutely - we'll run both and include eval metrics.
[07:58] Mark: Anything else on compliance? We need to ensure e-discovery and audit logs are accessible.
[08:03] Alex: Audit logs can be forwarded or pulled via API; retention settings are configurable. We'll include the details in the security pack.
[08:11] Priya: Okay I'll reiterate the info we'll need: sample inference dataset, exact p95/p99 targets, QPS profile over 24h, network/VPC contact, and any regulatory constraints.
[08:22] Daniel: I'll send network diagrams and the infra contact.
[08:25] Lisa: We'll share the sample dataset and expected traffic windows.
[08:28] Mark: Timeline - we want pilot in 2 weeks and a decision within 6 weeks if results look good.
[08:33] Alex: Sounds reasonable. We'll aim for that.
[08:36] Priya: Quick note on benchmarks - we'll simulate your QPS and provide token-level cost and latency percentiles; we recommend running end-to-end tests through your network to measure egress impact.
[08:47] Mark: OK. Any legal/procurement blockers we should know now?
[08:51] Alex: Standard MSA and DPA; for enterprise procurement we can fast-track with procurement templates.
[08:56] Lisa: One last thing - can we do a short technical deep dive with our infra team before the pilot?
[09:01] Priya: Yes, happy to do a 60-minute technical deep dive to go through VPC peering, image bootstrap, and autoscale hooks.
[09:08] Mark: Great. Let's recap next steps.
[09:11] Alex: We'll send: pricing tiers and examples, SOC 2 and security pack, pilot plan and benchmark schedule.
[09:18] Priya: And I'll prepare the benchmark plan and scripts, plus a technical-deep-dive agenda.
[09:24] Daniel: I'll email network diagrams and security contacts.
[09:27] Lisa: We'll send dataset and QPS profile.
[09:30] Mark: Thanks, everyone.
[57:20] (call end)
